summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 97.4% YoY to INR10,355.1 lakh, with EBITDA up 78% to INR1,703.9 lakh at a 16.5% margin.
summary.overview: Technocrats Plasma Systems reported H1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR10,355.1 lakh (up 97.4% YoY), EBITDA of INR1,703.9 lakh (16.5% margin) and PAT of INR1,194.8 lakh (11.5% margin, up 58%). Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of roughly 45-50% over FY26, which an analyst pointed out implies about INR195-200 crore. Working capital was stretched: trade receivables rose from about INR21 crore to INR68 crore and inventory from INR33 crore to INR53 crore, driving negative operating cash flow of about INR50 crore. Management tied the fix to moving outsourced site work in-house to a new 20,000 sq ft rented facility from December 2026.

segments.name: Machines with automation
segments.commentary: Contributed 22.5% of H1 FY27 revenue; management says automation and robotics (cobots, laser and plasma automation) are the growth thrust.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 45-50% over FY26 (management also cited 40-50% and 'minimum 35-40%' on product mix in one answer); management described this as a floor, with H2 seasonally stronger than H1.
Analyst-implied FY27 revenue of about INR195-200 crore; management said 'minimum 200' was the figure discussed.
Gross/EBITDA margin on in-house work expected at 40-50% versus 15-20% on outsourced site jobs, per management.
Plasma gasification: first small order of INR5-6 crore (sample order) expected in FY27; larger export orders expected to follow after proof of the sample.
RRCAT-linked indigenous fibre laser (defence): business expected to start after about 2 years; current order of about INR60 crore expected to execute in H2 FY27.
Working capital expected to improve as in-house manufacturing rises; management cited 80-90% advance or milestone payment in 2-3 years versus 90-120 day site cycles today.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation about 75%; 95 customers served in H1 FY27.
Rented facility expanding to 20,000 sq ft from 4,000 sq ft, with commercial production starting December 2026 and the old space surrendered in December.
Land identification under way for a proposed owned manufacturing facility to consolidate most manufacturing under one roof; no timeline given.

IPO proceeds of about INR60.98 crore: about INR21.2 lakh spent on capex, INR14.74 crore on working capital, and about INR34 crore yet to be deployed per management; management later said the INR34 crore was already deployed and sat in other current assets.
RRCAT fibre-laser technology transfer: PhD electronics engineer appointed to lead; main assembly and engineering to start the following month. BARC plasma gasification tie-up is also in progress.
demand_pricing: Management said input costs rose across the board due to the war, and some material was bought ahead for future projects; analyst noted material cost near 80% of H1 revenue.

Demand cited in shipbuilding, automobiles, infrastructure (INR5 lakh crore government infra spend cited), railways, defence, ONGC, oil and gas, steel plants, nuclear and heavy engineering; management sized its cutting and welding business at 6-7% of that infra spend.
Defence: robot installed at a defence equipment maker in Gujarat; cobot tie-up with a Chinese company for heavy and light fabrication, targeting shipbuilding.

Gasifier orders: initial customers expected to buy INR5-10 crore units, scaling to larger plants later; management said margins are unique but gave no number; an analyst's 40-45% EBIT framing was accepted as 'much higher'.
Management said most receivables come from tier-1 and tier-2 customers and described them as low risk; bill discounting being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Is 45-50% FY27 growth guidance conservative, given H1 growth of about 100%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 45-50% is a minimum assumption and upside would be additional; H2 is seasonally better than H1, agreed by management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential of the 20,000 sq ft facility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the space change has no direct link to revenue; the benefit is moving outsourced site jobs (15-20% margin) in-house (40-50% margin) and faster cash realisation versus 4-5 months on site jobs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables, inventory and other current assets rise sharply, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed receivables to 4-5 month site collection cycles and said inventory is ready-to-bill stock; the in-house factory is expected to fix this. The other current assets jump was described as IPO proceeds parked there, later said to be already deployed.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital cycle once larger customised systems are in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 60-day cycles in-house with 80-90% advances or milestone payments within 2-3 years, versus 90-120 days at project sites.

qa_highlights.question: Expected plasma gasification orders and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: A small INR5-6 crore sample order is expected in FY27; larger export orders to follow. Management did not quantify margins but said they are much higher than 40-45% EBIT.

qa_highlights.question: Why did material costs reach about 80% of revenue in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited war-driven input inflation across the board and extra material bought for future projects.

qa_highlights.question: Any related-party balance outstanding with Technodite (INR1.5 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing is pending; all related-party matters were settled before the IPO.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow was negative (about INR50 crore) in H1 despite operating profit, with receivables and inventory building sharply.
Management's guidance numbers varied across the call (45-50%, 40-50%, 35-40%); the FY27 absolute target was not firmly pinned down.
About INR34 crore of IPO proceeds: the answers on deployment were inconsistent (yet to be deployed versus already deployed, parked in other current assets).
Material cost near 80% of revenue in H1 amid input inflation; the gross margin figure was not provided.

Gasification and defence laser revenue depend on sample orders and multi-year timelines (laser business about 2 years away); top-three supplier details and the related-party query were not answered on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term growth, margins and new technologies, but evasive on quantification: several answers on gross margin, H2 versus H1 split, and industry size were deferred or not given. Working-capital and IPO-fund questions drew defensive answers that shifted explanation during the call.
